title: 12 · Java Swing GUI (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: building a stage

Console programs are a conversation: the program asks, you answer, in order. A GUI is a stage where the audience can do anything at any time, so Swing is event-driven: your code sits quietly and runs only when the user does something. Swing lives in javax.swing and is built on the older AWT (java.awt), so you usually import both.

The containment tree

JFrame is the picture frame (title bar, close button). JPanel is a tray you arrange things on. Components go on the tray: JLabel (read-only text), JTextField (type here, read with getText()), JPasswordField (dots; getPassword() returns char[]), JButton (clickable), JRadioButton (pick one, needs a ButtonGroup), JCheckBox (independent on/off). Use isSelected() on radio buttons and checkboxes.

Making a window appear

setSize(w,h), setDefaultCloseOperation(JFrame.EXIT_ON_CLOSE) (else closing the window leaves the program running), setLocationRelativeTo(null) to centre, and finally setVisible(true). Forget the last one and nothing shows.

Layout managers: the stage hands

Without one you would hand-place every pixel and everything breaks on resize. FlowLayout: left to right, wraps; JPanel's default. BorderLayout: NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST, CENTER (CENTER stretches); JFrame's default; one component per region, so put a JPanel in a region to hold several. GridLayout(rows, cols): equal cells filled left to right, top to bottom. CardLayout: stacked panels, one visible, switched with show(container, name), great for login then dashboard. Absolute positioning (setLayout(null) plus setBounds) works but is discouraged. Layouts can nest: a BorderLayout frame whose CENTER holds a GridLayout panel is the classic form.

Events: making buttons alive

A button does nothing until you attach an ActionListener, an object that waits for the click. btn.addActionListener(e -> { ... }); The code in braces runs on every click. e.getSource() tells you which component fired when one listener serves many buttons, and e.getActionCommand() gives the button's text (handy in a switch). A JTextField fires an action when Enter is pressed. Mouse activity uses MouseListener (pressed, released, clicked, entered, exited) and MouseMotionListener (dragged, moved); the Adapter classes let you override just one method. JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(frame, "text") pops up a message.

Reading input safely

getText() always returns a String. Convert with Integer.parseInt or Double.parseDouble and wrap it in try/catch for NumberFormatException so typing letters shows a friendly message instead of crashing.

GUI plus database

The classic Section C answer: GridLayout form in CENTER, Save button in a SOUTH panel, a listener that reads the fields, converts numbers, calls db.insert(...), and reports success or failure with JOptionPane.

Exam checklist

Imports. JFrame created and configured. Panel and layout chosen. Components added to the right regions. Listener attached with lambda. setVisible(true) last.
